newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Keppel, SPH to bid for Singapore telecoms licence.
newsitem.headline: Keppel, SPH to bid for Singapore telecoms licence.

text.p: Diversified maritime company Keppel Corp said on Wednesday it would join forces with newspaper group Singapore Press Holdings to bid for a licence to operate a full telecoms service in Singapore when the industry is deregulated in 2000.
The Straits Times newspaper on Wednesday quoted Keppel chairman Sim Kee Boon as telling reporters the two companies had not yet decided on a foreign partner for their bid.
A Keppel spkeswoman confirmed the newspaper report.
"He was asked if Keppel and SPH would bid together for a full licence. He said 'Yes'," she said.
SPH officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
Keppel and SPH are already partners in MobileOne, Singapore's second mobile telephone and pager service, due to start operations on April 1, 1997.
Another member of the MobileOne consortium, Cable and Wireless, told Reuters on Tuesday it would "definitely" bid for a licence but had not yet decided on its local partner.

Singapore said in September it would allow at least one, and possibly two, new operators to compete directly with the current monopoly telephone company, Singapore Telecom, from April 2000. Foreign firms must have a 51 percent local partner.
Two Singapore state-owned firms, Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT) and Singapore Power, announced a bid for a full licence on Monday.
Several foreign companies, including British Telecom Plc, AT&T of the United States and Deutsche Telekom are all considering bids, industry sources say.
Both Keppel and SPH are government linked.
